meta.title: Adam Ferreira — Software Engineer · Dev & QA Automation
meta.description: Adam Ferreira's CV: software engineer, mobile development and test automation (Flutter, Appium, iOS, Android).

identity.headline: Software Engineer · Dev & QA Automation
identity.tagline: I work on what makes a mobile app testable: framework, CI, test data through APIs, test IDs in the code, tooling for the teams.

experience.intro: Betclic is rebuilding its iOS and Android app in Flutter. I automate the tests of the gamification features: missions and challenges, leaderboards, reward games, and boosts offered when placing a bet. The tests live in a repo shared between mobile and web.
experience.lead: Mobile test automation for the gamification of Betclic's new Flutter app, 5 million players.
experience.subtitle: Building the automation alongside the app
experience.subintro: When I joined, the app and its gamification features were still being built. The tests had to keep up with each release without slowing the developers down.

bullets.title: Testability built into the app code
bullets.short: 143 pull requests merged in six months, 44 of them in the Flutter app: semantics that make each screen testable, and fixes for bugs I found.
bullets.text: 143 PRs merged in six months, 44 in the Flutter app: semantics and bug fixes.

bullets.title: Test data seeded through backend APIs
bullets.short: Bets are placed and settled through APIs before each scenario. The UI only serves what the test checks.
bullets.text: bets placed and settled before each scenario; the UI only for what the test checks.

bullets.title: The gamification E2E suite, built from scratch
bullets.short: I wrote the first gamification scenario and set up its nightly run. Six months later, 86 scenarios run on Android and iOS: each one checks something the product needs, none is there for the count.
bullets.text: 86 scenarios in six months, run nightly, each tied to a product need.

bullets.title: Root causes traced down to iOS, Android and Flutter
bullets.short: When a test failed for the wrong reason, I followed the cause into the iOS accessibility tree, Android's system bars or the Flutter widget tree, and fixed it in the framework instead of adding retries.
bullets.text: false failures fixed in the framework, never hidden behind retries.

bullets.title: Regression tests beyond gamification
bullets.short: I also automate regression tests outside gamification, social and betting among them. They run in the release train, on several regulated markets, before every version.
bullets.text: social and betting included, run in the release train.

experience.intro: ALL is Accor's hotel booking and loyalty app (100 million members). I automated the tests of its member area (sign-in, status, rewards, deals) and, beyond my scope, kept improving the test framework shared by its three squads (loyalty, booking, stay).
experience.lead: Mobile test automation for the member area of ALL, Accor's booking and loyalty app, 100 million members.
experience.subtitle: Modernizing an existing framework

bullets.title: A test framework shared by three squads
bullets.short: Java 25 and Appium upgrades, dead code cleared out, over 250 feature files reworked across the three squads, and per-scenario logs in IntelliJ even in parallel runs, a gap JetBrains still hasn't closed.
bullets.text: Java 25, per-scenario logs in parallel runs, 250+ feature files reworked.

bullets.title: Explicit waits instead of fixed pauses
bullets.short: Waits that poll the screen, in the helper all three squads share: a test moves on as soon as the app is ready. The goal: shorter runs.
bullets.text: polling waits in the helper all squads share, to shorten runs.

bullets.title: Ten different devices in parallel
bullets.short: The 10 parallel sessions all ran on the same device model. Now each runs on a different BrowserStack device, so bugs specific to a model, a tablet or an orientation show up.
bullets.text: 10 parallel sessions, now each on a different device: model and orientation bugs surface.

bullets.title: A rewritten CI with a 90% quality gate
bullets.short: The old pipeline stayed green whatever happened. The new one fails below a 90% pass rate and tells each team on Slack.
bullets.text: reports to Jira and Xray, alerts each team on Slack.

bullets.title: Hard-to-reach paths under test
bullets.short: Features behind flags, store builds from TestFlight and Firebase, webviews behind the company firewall: the paths a test suite usually can't reach.
bullets.text: feature flags, store builds, TestFlight and Firebase distributions, webviews behind the WAF.

bullets.title: A TypeScript alternative, prototyped from scratch
bullets.short: WebdriverIO and Cucumber, one codebase for iOS and Android, multi-locale, with a documented comparison against the Java stack.
bullets.text: WebdriverIO, cross-platform and multi-locale, compared with Java.

experience.intro: Built features for Hexaly Studio, a low-code React SaaS for optimization problems (delivery planning, warehouse management).

bullets.title: Three features shipped
bullets.text: a Highcharts pie chart widget, resizable widgets, clickable error links in the Xterm.js terminal.

experience.intro: For Maintenance Industrie (industrial cleaning): a SaaS to manage its sites and a mobile time-clock app for its staff.

bullets.title: At the origin of JMD's product
bullets.text: their field-service platform (planning, clock-in, proof of service) grew out of it.

bullets.title: First SaaS release
bullets.text: delivered and validated by the client at the end of the internship; code review before every merge.

bullets.title: Kept on as a freelancer
bullets.text: built the companion mobile app in Flutter, with Riverpod and Dio.
